This criminal revision petition under Section 397 read with 401 Cr.P.C. has been preferred against the judgment dated 29.11.2008 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge No.2, Jodhpur in Criminal Appeal No. 162/2007, wherein the order of conviction and sentence dated 22.06.2007 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Jodhpur in Original Criminal Case No. 420/2004 was confirmed.
2.

] Offences Under Section Sentences 324/34 IPC One year's R.I. with fine of Rs.5000/-
and in default of payment of fine to further undergo three months' S.I.

3 . As per the prosecution's case, on 02.05.2004, the complainant - Sitaram submitted a written report before the SHO of Police Station Mandore, Jodhpur alleging inter alia that on 01.05.2004, at around 11:30 P.M., the petitioners threw acid on the complainant and injured persons, who were going to Kumbheshwar Mahadev Temple.
In the aforesaid incident, Pintu, Babulal and Jayesh got severely burned.
4. On the basis of this aforesaid report, an FIR No. 102/2004 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 307 and 324/34 of the IPC and the investigation was commenced.

After filing of charge sheet and upon completion of trial, the petitioners were convicted by the learned trial court below for the offence under Section 324/34 of the IPC vide judgment dated 22.06.2007 which was upheld by the learned Appellate Court vide judgment dated 29.11.2008.

5. Learned counsel for the revisionist-petitioners submitted that the sentences so awarded to the revisionist-petitioners were suspended by this Court, vide order dated 02.12.2008 in S.B.Cr. Misc.
Bail (Suspension of Sentence) Application No.447/2008.

S.B.Cr. Misc.

sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners have already undergone detention for some period and case is pending against them since 2004.
It was further submitted [2025:RJ-JD:30777] (3 of 4) [CRLR-1279/2008] that the petitioners have been facing the agony of a long and protracted trial.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioners, in the alternate, has prayed that without making any interference on merits/conviction, the sentences so awarded to the present revisionist-petitioners may be substituted with the period of sentences already undergone by them.
8. Per Contra, learned Public Prosecutor opposes the submissions made on behalf of the petitioners.
However, he was not in a position to dispute that the present revision petition is pending since 2008.

9. Heard.
10.
A perusal of the impugned judgments makes it manifest that the alleged incident happened in the year 2004 and the present revision petition is pending adjudication since 2008.

11. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Alister Anthony Pareira Vs. State of Maharashtra reported in (2012)2 SCC 648 and Haripada Das Vs. State of W.B. reported in (1998)9 SCC 678, was pleased to observe as under:

2 Alister Anthony Pareira (supra) "There is no straitjacket formula for sentencing an accused on proof of crime.

sentences.text: The courts have evolved certain principles: twin objective of the sentencing policy is deterrence and correction.

What sentence would meet the ends of justice depends on the facts and circumstances of each case and the court must keep in mind the gravity of the crime, motive for the circumstances."
[2025:RJ-JD:30777] (4 of 4) [CRLR-1279/2008] Haripada Das (supra)
"

...considering the fact that the respondent had case is pending for a pretty long time for which he had already undergone detention for some period and the suffered both financial hardship and mental agony and also considering the fact that he had been released on bail as far back as on 17-1-1986, we feel that the ends of justice will be met in the facts of the case if the sentence is reduced to the period already undergone..."
12. In the light of aforesaid discussion and precedent law and keeping in view the limited prayer made on behalf of the present petitioners, this revision petition is partly allowed.

13. Accordingly, while maintaining the conviction of the petitioners for the offence under Section 324/34 of IPC, the sentences awarded to them are hereby reduced to the period already undergone by them.
The petitioners are on bail.
They need not surrender.
Their bail bonds stand discharged accordingly.
14. All pending applications (if any) also stand disposed of accordingly.
15. Record of the case be sent back to the learned court below forthwith.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 22-divya/-
